concepts.description: Every business object the use case handles, matched to the ontology.

object.description: The business object, as step 4 named it.

id.description: The ontology concept it matches, by its id exactly as the ontology gives it. Required unless the status is gap.

status.description: matched = the concept exists and fits as is · partial = it exists but covers only part of what is needed · enhancement = it exists and needs extending (an attribute, a state, a relationship) · gap = not in the ontology: an ontology delta.

note.description: What is partial, what the enhancement is, or why it is a gap.

name.description: For a gap: the proposed concept's name.

module.description: For a gap: the ontology module it belongs in.

kind.description: For a gap: its kind, in the ontology's own kinds.

definition.description: For a gap: a one-line definition the Ontology Council can review.

relationships.description: Relationships the use case ADDS or CHANGES — existing ones between matched concepts are drawn without being listed.

subject.description: A concept id, or a gap's object name.

object.description: A concept id, or a gap's object name.
